chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who led a group in prayer and prayed one rak'ah with them, then died. He said: 'They should appoint another man, count the rak'ah as valid, place the deceased behind them, and whoever touched him must perform ghusl.' And whoever did not catch the takbirah of ruku' has missed that rak'ah. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةُ الرُّكُوعِ: Takbirah of ruku' (the saying of Allahu Akbar when bowing)

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings when an imam dies during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the continuity of congregational prayer (*salat al-jama'ah*) despite the sudden death of the imam, emphasizing that the missed rak'ah is not nullified but rather completed by the successor. It further details the practical ritual purity implications, requiring *ghusl* for those who touched the deceased imam, thereby linking the physical reality of death to the spiritual validity of the ongoing worship. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of the prayer depends on the continuity of the act rather than the uninterrupted presence of a single living leader.
